technical.clientSecretHandling: Confidential server-side client. The token endpoint accepts the Client ID and Client Secret via HTTP Basic (client_secret_basic) or POST body (client_secret_post). Keep the secret on your server; the app assessment questionnaire asks how you store it.

refreshTokens.expiry: Read x_refresh_token_expires_in from every token response. Intuit sources disagree on the policy: older docs describe a 100-day inactivity expiry, and an Intuit blog post (not fetchable) describes a five-year maximum.
refreshTokens.notes: Rotates: always store the refresh token from the latest response. The previous one may stop working immediately.

redirectUriRules: Must be registered in the Developer Portal for the environment (Development and Production keys have separate redirect URI lists)
Production redirect URIs must use HTTPS; plain-http localhost works only with Development (sandbox) keys
Intuit's redirect URI page reportedly also bans IP addresses for production (seen only in a search snippet)

profiles.intent: Read accounting data for users' companies

scopes.name: com.intuit.quickbooks.accounting
scopes.purpose: QuickBooks Online Accounting API access (CompanyInfo, reports, transactions). Also makes the callback include the realm ID for the connected company.

testModeLimits.text: Development keys work only against sandbox companies, so no real customer can connect until production keys are unblocked. You get up to 10 free sandbox companies, each valid for two years.

configGotchas.text: Development and production keys, and their redirect URIs, are separate. Dev keys fail against live companies and vice versa.
Refresh tokens rotate. Save the new refresh token after every refresh, and serialize refreshes per company to avoid invalid_grant races.
Production redirect URIs must be HTTPS; a localhost callback only works with development keys.
Read calls are CorePlus (metered). On the free Builder tier they're reportedly blocked after 500,000 per month, counted across all production apps in your workspace.

stage1.summary: Self-serve: create an app, pick the accounting scope, use the Development keys against the sandbox company you get with a developer account, and complete one code flow.

stage2.summary: Before any real company can connect you need production keys, which stay blocked until Intuit accepts your app details (EULA, privacy policy, app URLs) and the app assessment questionnaire. This applies to unlisted apps too. Reads also fall under metered CorePlus calls, which are free only up to the Builder cap.

time.startsWhen: after you submit the app assessment questionnaire with all app details filled in

stage1DoneWhen.text: GET https://sandbox-quickbooks.api.intuit.com/v3/company/{realmId}/companyinfo/{realmId} with Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN and Accept: application/json returns 200 with the sandbox company's CompanyInfo, and your token response included a refresh_token.

blockedBy.how: Keeps production keys blocked until it accepts the app details and app assessment questionnaire. It can ask for more information, re-review apps every year, and block CorePlus (read) calls above the Builder monthly cap.

Each QuickBooks company is authorized separately, and you get a token plus realm ID per company. It's believed, but not sourced, that only a company admin can connect apps. Disconnecting from QuickBooks revokes the token.
Missing app URLs, EULA or privacy policy, or a questionnaire answer such as not having tested connect, disconnect and reconnect in sandbox, can block or reject production access.

profiles.bottomLine: You can get a sandbox token in one sitting. Real customers need production keys, which Intuit unblocks only after reviewing your app details and assessment questionnaire, even if you never list the app. Also budget for reads: they're metered CorePlus calls, free only up to the Builder cap.
topRisks: Production keys stay blocked until Intuit accepts the questionnaire; there is no official timeline
Read-heavy syncs can hit the Builder tier's CorePlus cap (about 500,000 per month), after which calls are blocked unless you pay for a tier
Rotating refresh tokens plus concurrent workers cause invalid_grant and forced reconnects

steps.title: Create the app in the Intuit Developer Portal
instructions: Sign in at https://developer.intuit.com (an Intuit Developer account comes with a sandbox company).
Open your app dashboard (the Apps tab in your Workspace, or My Hub > App dashboard) and click the + tile.
Select QuickBooks Online and Payments as the app type, click Next, name the app and click Next.

links.label: Create and start developing your app

steps.title: Select the accounting scope
instructions: On the permissions screen, select com.intuit.quickbooks.accounting and click Done.
Leave out com.intuit.quickbooks.payment unless you process payments. Add openid, email or profile only if you also want Intuit sign-in.

steps.title: Register a Development redirect URI
instructions: In the app's settings, open Settings > Redirect URIs and make sure you're editing Development, not Production.
Add your callback exactly as your code sends it, e.g. http://localhost:8000/callback. Plain-http localhost is fine for development keys only.
Click Save.

steps.title: Copy the Development Client ID and Client Secret
instructions: On the app's keys page (named Keys & OAuth, Keys, or Keys and credentials depending on the source), make sure the Development set is selected.
Turn on Show credentials if the secret is hidden, then copy the Client ID and Client Secret.
Store the secret only on your server or in a secret manager.

links.label: Get the Client ID and Client Secret

steps.title: Send yourself through the authorize URL
instructions: Open https://appcenter.intuit.com/connect/oauth2?client_id=CLIENT_ID&response_type=code&scope=com.intuit.quickbooks.accounting&redirect_uri=YOUR_URI&state=RANDOM
Sign in, pick your sandbox company and approve.
On the callback, check that state matches. Keep the code and the realm ID, which is the company ID for every API call. The realm ID is only returned for the Accounting and Payments scopes.
PKCE isn't covered in the Intuit sources read, so use the confidential-client flow with the secret on your server.

steps.title: Exchange the code for tokens
instructions: POST to https://oauth.platform.intuit.com/oauth2/v1/tokens/bearer with grant_type=authorization_code, the code and the same redirect_uri.
Authenticate with HTTP Basic (Client ID:Client Secret) or as POST parameters; both are listed in the discovery document.
Store access_token (valid 3600 seconds), refresh_token, x_refresh_token_expires_in and the realm ID, keyed by company.

steps.title: Call CompanyInfo on the sandbox company
instructions: GET https://sandbox-quickbooks.api.intuit.com/v3/company/{realmId}/companyinfo/{realmId} with Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN and Accept: application/json.
Expect 200 with CompanyInfo. Log the intuit_tid response header for support requests.

steps.title: Refresh and save the rotated refresh token
instructions: When the access token expires, refresh with grant_type=refresh_token at the same token endpoint.
Replace the stored refresh token with the one in the response every time; the previous one may stop working immediately.
Allow only one refresh in flight per company. Treat invalid_grant as needing a reconnect, not as a retryable error.

steps.title: Fill in production app details
instructions: Verify your Intuit Developer profile and email.
Add the end-user license agreement and privacy policy URLs.
Add the host domain, launch URL (the page in your app where users connect to QuickBooks) and disconnect URL.
If the Reconnect URL field appears in app settings (from 2026-02-24), fill it in with the page where customers reconnect.

steps.title: Test connect, disconnect and reconnect in sandbox
instructions: Connect a sandbox company, disconnect it, and reconnect it, and check that your app handles each step.
Exercise expired access tokens, expired refresh tokens, invalid_grant and CSRF (state) errors. The questionnaire asks about each.

steps.title: Complete the app assessment questionnaire
instructions: Open the production side of the app. Sources name the entry point differently: Production Settings > App assessment questionnaire, Keys and credentials (Production) > Compliance > Start questionnaire, or App Overview > Get production keys.
Answer the sections (app information, authorization, API usage, accounting API, error handling, security). It takes 30-40 minutes, and you can save partway through.
You need one questionnaire per app. It's required even if the app will never be listed on the QuickBooks App Store.
Submit, and answer any follow-up requests from Intuit.

steps.title: Copy production keys and add an HTTPS redirect URI
instructions: Once unblocked, copy the Production Client ID and Client Secret. These are a different pair from the Development keys.
Under Redirect URIs, with Production selected, add your HTTPS callback and save.
Point the authorize and token flow at production and call the production API host (believed to be quickbooks.api.intuit.com, not sourced).

steps.title: Watch CorePlus (read) usage against your tier
instructions: Reads, queries and reports are reportedly CorePlus calls. Only successful 2xx calls are metered, summed across all production apps in your workspace.
On the free Builder tier, CorePlus calls above the monthly allowance (about 500,000) are blocked.
To go beyond it, move to a paid tier (Silver and up) by adding a payment method in the Developer Portal. Use filtered queries, change data capture (CDC) and webhooks to cut reads.

nuances.text: Developer docs render only in a browser, and portal labels change often; expect differences from this guide.
Every connected QuickBooks company is a separate authorization with its own tokens and realm ID. The realm ID goes in the API path twice for CompanyInfo.
Refresh token lifetime is inconsistent across Intuit sources (24 hours to 5 years). Trust x_refresh_token_expires_in in each response.
Design for the old refresh token to stop working immediately after a refresh.

Production keys (questionnaire) and App Store listing (technical, security and marketing review) are separate. Listing isn't required for other companies to connect, and the long waits are for listing, not keys.
The production entry point may be labelled Production Settings, Keys and credentials (Production toggle), App Overview > Get production keys, or App settings.
Intuit publishes separate sandbox and production discovery documents. The questionnaire asks whether you use them for current endpoints.
Intuit's Python OAuth library notes its endpoints work only with TLS 1.2.
Approval isn't one-off. Listed apps and apps with over 500 connections are reportedly re-reviewed every year, with two weeks to fix flagged issues.
